q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT beer.name, MIN(serves.price) AS min_price, (SELECT serves.bar FROM serves WHERE serves.beer = beer.name LIMIT 1) AS bar FROM beer LEFT JOIN serves ON serves.beer = beer.name GROUP BY beer.name

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT beer.name, MIN(serves.price) AS min_price, (SELECT serves.bar FROM serves WHERE serves.beer = beer.name LIMIT 1) AS bar FROM beer LEFT JOIN serves ON serves.beer = beer.name GROUP BY beer.name

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they join the 'serves' table in different ways, which can lead to different results when there are multiple rows in 'serves' for the same beer and bar.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when a beer is served by multiple bars at the same price. In this case, Q1 will return all bars that serve the beer at the minimum price, while Q2 will only return the first bar that serves the beer at the minimum price.
